correctness.rationale: Exact proof: lattice rounding proves μ=1. Every candidate packet radius strictly below sqrt(3/2) would have every subset sum norm squared <=4 by even norms. Exactly 48 eligible D4 generators; exhaustive exact Gram recursion has independent prefixes 1,48,816,1728,0, excluding every rank-4 frame. A determinant-two basis and 24 exact midpoint-ball certificates (12 squared radius one, 12 squared radius three-halves) meet the lower bound. The finite exhaustive search is complete only because the proved short-vector cutoff reduces an infinite statement to finite possibilities.

value.rationale: The recently introduced invariant measures a substantive geometry-of-numbers cost of using one common frame instead of arbitrary lattice triangulations. The naturally canonical 4D root lattice has a sharp explicit gap sqrt(3/2) versus ordinary radius one, accompanied by an exact universal subset-sum extremum and a matching basis. This addresses a clear low-dimensional gap left by the motivating asymptotic theorem and offers reusable finite certification geometry, not a routine special case of a known exact formula.
